data.raw_text:
On this day, July 16th, in history:

1054- The Great Schism began when Cardinal Humbert of Rome placed a bull of excommunication against Patriarch Cerularius of Constantinople, placing the edict against the Patriarch on the altar of the Hagia Sophia itself.

1216- Pope Innocent III died at the age of 55 from a fever. Innocent III is most known for the infamous debacles that were the 4th and 5th crusades.

1228- Francis of Assisi was canonized as a saint two years after his death by Pope Gregory IX.

1377- King Richard II of England was crowned at the age of 10, following the death of his grandfather King Edward III.

1519- The debate at Leipzig (current day Germany) ended with Martin Luther publicly debating Johann Eck, during which Luther denied the Devine right of the Pope.

1769- The first Catholic mission is dedicated in current day California by Spanish Franciscan missionary Junípero Serra, in current day San Diego.

1779- American Brigadier General “Mad” Anthony Wayne earned his moniker by leading a surprise attack on the heavily fortified British position at Stony Point, New York.

1790- The US Congress signed the Residence Act which announced the creation of a new national capital was to be built on the swampy Potomac River and named Washington D.C..

1882- US First Lady Mary Todd Lincoln died at the age of 63 from a stroke.

1918- In the middle of the night the 50 year old deposed Tsar Nicholas II and 10 other members of his family were lined up in their home confinement in Yekaterinburg, Russia, when the Bolshevik soldiers keeping them prisoner opened fire on them. It is reported that the Tsar’s daughters had jewel encrusted corsets which protected them from the initial barrage of bullets, causing their executioners to further use pistols and bayonets to dispatch them, leading many to believe that the youngest, Princess Anastasia, may have survived and multiple people would claim to be her. This ended the Romanov Dynasty which had ruled Russia for over 3 centuries, and had held sway in Russia as nobles for even longer.

1935- The first ever Parking Meter is installed in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

1945- The first ever atomic bomb was successfully detonated by the Manhattan Project at 5:29:45 am at Trinity Site in Alamogordo, New Mexico.

1951- The novel “Catcher in the Rye” is published by J.D. Salinger.

1967- Actor Will Ferrell was born in Irvine, California.

1969- Apollo 11 successfully launched from Cape Kennedy, Florida at 9:32 am EDT, the first ever successful lunar mission.

1973- Amidst the live Senate hearings on the Watergate Scandal, it was revealed that there had been a secret recording device taping all of President Richard Nixon’s phone calls and in person conversations in the White House.

1979- Iraqi President Ahmed Hassan Al-Bakr resigned and announced that he would be succeeded by the infamous Saddam Hussein. 

Also 1979- Doctor Jeffrey MacDonald’s trial began in North Carolina to determine if he had been the one to kill his two daughters and wife, an incident which happened nearly a decade earlier.

1990- Over 1,000 people are killed by a 7.7 magnitude earthquake in the Philippines. 

1999- 38 year old JFK Jr and his wife Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, as well as Carolyn’s sister Lauren Bessette, all died when the plane JFK Jr was piloting malfunctioned and crashed above the Atlantic Ocean, near Martha’s Vineyard.

2002- US President George W Bush announced his plan to strengthen homeland security following the aftermath of September 11, 2001.

2005- The novel “Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince” was published by J.K. Rowling, the 6th book in the series.

2017- American-Canadian director George A. Romero died at the age of 77 from lung cancer. He was best known as the “Father of the Zombie Film” genre.
